claim: Matching original retail DLL source proves a concrete texture-sprite code path. PartsInfoManager.GetPartsFileName MethodDef0x060010CD uses source strings 'PartsTex/' and '/', GetHighlightPartsFileName MethodDef0x060010CE uses '_h'; PartsInfoManager.LoadPartsTex MethodDef0x060010D0 checks '.png', calls GetCraftPartsFilePath/Pnt_PaintToolIO.LoadImageData on its craft branch, and GetPartsFileName/UnityEngine.Resources.Load on its resource branch. FormRenderer.LoadPartsTex MethodDef0x06001F23 calls PartsInfoManager.LoadPartsTex and sets partsTex; FormRenderer.InitSprite MethodDef0x06001F20 obtains partsTex and calculates the rectangle via CalcPartsRect MethodDef0x06001F28, then calls original UnityEngine.Sprite.Create and SpriteRenderer.set_sprite. Exact six method-body SHAs, seven byte-window SHAs, four source strings, Unity member references and IL opcode sites prove the source relationships. No specific rendered asset or playback execution is established.
